title: The Lowest Closing Price as an In-Place Home Resale Asking Price
content:
**The lowest closing price — In-Place Home Resale.** A seller whose home is listed may ask for the asking price to be set at the lowest closing price, the lowest asking price at which a sale would still close with every closing deduction paid from the proceeds; the seller signs that price change and the asking price becomes exactly that figure.

## Conditions of the price

Before the lowest closing price is worked out, the file's ledger must carry the appraisal fee owed for every appraisal recorded on the file.

On the Guaranteed Resale Program the asking price may never exceed the package's highest list price as a percentage of the appraised value, so where the lowest closing price would exceed that ceiling no asking price lets a sale close: the asking price is left as it stands and the request goes to a human representative.

| Situation | Result |
|---|---|
| home listed; the file's ledger carries the appraisal fee owed for every appraisal recorded on the file | the lowest closing price is worked out and the seller signs it as the new asking price |
| Guaranteed Resale Program; lowest closing price above the package's list-price ceiling | asking price left as it stands; the request goes to a human representative |

## Invocation

The price change is made with `set_asking_price_9cfe4b28`, a tool owned by the seller: the agent unlocks it and hands it over, and the customer themselves runs it to sign the new asking price for their own listed home on the spot. One call replaces the file's current asking price with the new one; the listing dates, the term and everything else on the file stay as they were, and the seller sees the new asking price on the file and on the listing.

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `resale_id` | the resale file number of the seller's listed home, as read to the seller from the in-place resale file lookup | identifier text |
| `new_list_price` | the new asking price, in USD | a positive number with 2 decimal places; recorded exactly as passed |

## Return

On success the tool returns a text rendering of these fields: `status` (the text "price_changed"), `resale_id` (the file changed), `previous_list_price` (the asking price replaced, USD with 2 decimal places) and `list_price` (the asking price now on the file, USD with 2 decimal places). The tool defines no other receipt.
